comments.author: @Top10Documentary999
comments.text: A city can build skyscrapers, expand its economy, and still fail its people in the most basic way. 🇧🇩 Seeing families living beside a river this polluted raises a difficult question: should economic development ever come at the cost of people's health and dignity? What is the point of progress if ordinary people are left breathing the consequences

replies.author: @UnseenPlanett
replies.text: That question stays with us too. Progress means little if the people building it can't breathe clean air. The most surprising part? Many of those families still welcome visitors with tea and a smile. Thanks for adding such depth to the conversation!

comments.author: @EarthRevealed-e1b
comments.text: Watching this really changed the way I see Bangladesh. It's heartbreaking to see people working so hard just to survive, especially the children and those risking their lives in dangerous jobs. What struck me most is how families can spend years building a home and lose everything overnight. These people deserve more than just survival. They deserve safety, dignity, and a better future. Respect to the people of Bangladesh!

replies.author: @UnseenPlanett
replies.text: Thank you for this beautiful comment! The strength and warmth of the people in Bangladesh is what moved us most while making this. And there are even more untold stories from this part of the world coming soon, so stay tuned!

comments.author: @AmazingDiscoveriesTopUS
comments.text: The stories of sewage cleanes and garment workers really stayed with me. No one should have to risk their life just to earn a living.

replies.author: @UnseenPlanett
replies.text: Those stories stayed with us too. Many sewage workers in Dhaka go down with almost no protection, just to keep the city running every single day. Thank you for watching with such an open heart!
